external_simulator.characterization_scope: Historical official four-block OSSOS-B characterization present immediately before its removal from the repository; this is not the complete eight-block OSSOS survey.

wrong_model.interpretation: Deliberately wrong phenomenological Neptune-barrier alternative concentrated near q=30 AU; it is not a physical no-Planet-X model.

scientific_scope: Independently repeat the locked JX-O1 telescope-selection calibration with fresh intrinsic populations, fresh official-simulator random seeds, and fresh resampling streams while leaving the V2 thresholds, population laws, sample targets, and V3 exact finite-pool zeta method unchanged.
limitations: The inherited v1 contract schema requires the registration token PRELOCKED_BEFORE_ANY_JX_O1_OUTCOMES. For this V4 record it means prelocked before any V4 outcome; V1 through V3 outcomes were already known.
V4 copies every V2 scientific threshold and target unchanged and selects the V3 exact finite-pool zeta formula before generating any V4 telescope outcome.

Independence is computational: the intrinsic-population HMAC key, official-driver seed domain, resampling key, execution checkpoints, raw files, and registered pool hashes are new. The telescope characterization and population laws are intentionally held fixed for direct replication.
The V4 finalizer rejects any manifest hash or normalized semantic detection-pool hash that matches the official V2 pools.
This validation uses the historical four-block OSSOS-B characterization at the pinned official commit, not the complete eight-block OSSOS release or the full affiliated-survey ensemble.
The runner uses 100001-object batches because the pinned ReadModelFromFile EOF path is invalid when the final internal 100-object chunk is exactly full.
The correct and wrong populations are calibration distributions, not competing physical formation histories.
The wrong model is deliberately strong and phenomenological; passing the power gate does not establish power for realistic Planet X alternatives.
The inclination law is explicitly a truncated half-normal, not a fitted observed-TNO inclination distribution.
The adopted Lawler et al. divot has alpha_bright=0.9, alpha_faint=0.5, break H_r=8.3, and contrast 3.2 over the locked finite H range 5 to 12.
Only r-band characterization is used; non-r colors are declared but do not affect the pinned OSSOS-B efficiency files.
Mock catalogs contain 20 detections and are used for method calibration, not as the observed Solar System.
No pilot outcome can satisfy the official-backend gate; only fresh official OSSOS tracked outputs can support the V4 verdict.
External OSSOS code remains under EUPL-1.1 and is executed separately rather than copied into the MIT JX source tree.
nonclaim: A PASSED V4 verdict independently confirms the locked JX-O1 computational telescope-selection calibration on fresh random populations. It does not detect or exclude Planet X, validate any candidate source, establish power for realistic Planet X alternatives, or show that either calibration population describes the Solar System.

allowed_verdicts.PASSED: Fresh official pools pass every unchanged calibration, power, scale, adapter-identity, provenance, independence, seed-stability, exact-moment, and exact-replay gate.
allowed_verdicts.BLOCKED: The independent method is numerically valid but required external execution, sample scale, checkpoint proof, or wrong-model power is incomplete.
allowed_verdicts.INVALID: Input integrity, pool independence, finite-record, statistical calibration, adapter identity, seed stability, or deterministic replay fails.
